angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 366,634 km at 46.06 pc = 0.11 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 21.7092 +/- 0.0099 mas (same row, RUWE 1.00): 46.06 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.527 +/- 0.021 solar radii from Harris et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-904 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...959L...1H/abstract): 366,634 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.557 +/- 0.028 solar masses from Harris et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-904 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...959L...1H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3770.2 +/- 70 K from Harris et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-904 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...959L...1H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Harris et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-904 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...959L...1H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-904.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.740, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
